summary: In international space exploration, the joint European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrived in orbit around Mercury today, marking a major planetary science milestone. Meanwhile, civil space operations face technical setbacks on Mars, where NASA’s Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter have temporarily halted science activities due to glitches, though the Curiosity rover remains active, recently collecting physical samples and photographing drifting twilight clouds. In military space defense, a U.S. intelligence report revealed that Russia is developing a nuclear space weapon, prompting the U.S. Senate to prepare an investigation into Ukraine’s access to SpaceX’s Starshield communications platform, while the Department of the Air Force is fast-tracking a new Space Data Network to maintain secure Joint Force connectivity. In launch and commercial space operations, SpaceX executed a classified launch for the U.S. Space Force from California and safely recovered a Dragon cargo capsule returning from the International Space Station; additionally, Chief Executive Elon Musk announced plans to retire the first Starship upper stage successfully caught by launch tower arms. On the commercial front, RBC Signals secured $10 million in funding to commercialize satellite communication technologies, while startup Atomic-6 outlined plans to build astronaut shielding against untrackable orbital debris. In astronomical science, researchers verified the first direct image captured of a black hole, published Fermi’s 14-year all-sky map bridging the gamma-ray "MeV gap," and traced the origin of Europa’s sodium cloud to its internal ocean. Looking ahead, observers should monitor NASA’s forthcoming updates on troubleshooting efforts to restore full science operations across its Mars fleet.
